purpose: Concrete, reusable conflict situations — different from story_patterns.json (which is structural shape). One moral can pair with many conflicts from here to avoid the repetition documented in phase3/knowledge/failures/repeated_story.md.

conflicts.name: Lost toy
Sharing toys with a sibling or friend
Breaking a small promise by accident
Waiting impatiently for something
Helping a grandparent with a small task
Not wanting to clean up after playing
Feeling scared of the dark
Meeting a new friend at school
Finding a lost kitten or animal
A rainy day changes the day's plan
Wanting to say something that isn't quite true to avoid trouble
A trip to the market and forgetting something important
Forgetting to say salam to a neighbor
Wanting a toy that isn't yours at a store
A friend not wanting to play the game you chose
Feeling left out at a birthday party
Spilling something and worrying about getting in trouble
Not wanting to share the last snack
A sibling breaking something of yours by accident
Getting briefly separated in a crowded place
Not wanting to wake up for the morning routine
A new sibling getting a lot of attention
Losing a game and feeling upset
Not wanting to clean up after a long play session
A friend saying something unkind by accident
Feeling scared to try something new, like swimming
Wanting extra time doing something fun before stopping
Forgetting a small responsibility, like feeding a pet
A stray animal needing gentle help
Moving to a new house and missing old friends
Winning a game and bragging about it
conflicts.notes: Character wins fairly, then boasts, and sees a friend's face fall.

conflicts.name: Being asked to pray while in the middle of fun play
conflicts.notes: Real, common tension between play and salah timing, age-appropriate.

conflicts.name: Not wanting to wash hands or brush teeth
conflicts.notes: Classic, real, universally relatable.

conflicts.name: A classmate has less than you at lunchtime
conflicts.notes: Concrete, visible-need charity scenario for young children.

conflicts.name: Wanting to interrupt while someone else is talking
conflicts.notes: Direct fit for good-speech/patience-in-listening.

conflicts.name: A friend from a different background joins the class
conflicts.notes: Real, inclusive scenario without stereotyping — friendship theme.

conflicts.name: Getting frustrated during wudu because it's cold or slow
conflicts.notes: Concrete daily-practice friction point.

conflicts.name: A pet needs feeding but character is busy playing
conflicts.notes: Distinct from cf_028 (forgetting) — here it's active choice to delay, not forgetting.

conflicts.name: Overhearing gossip about a friend and deciding whether to repeat it
conflicts.notes: Real good-speech dilemma about not spreading unkind talk.

conflicts.name: A family member is sick and routines change
conflicts.notes: Gentle, age-appropriate family-care scenario — no death/serious illness detail, just 'not feeling well.'

conflicts.name: Wanting to skip helping set up for a family gathering
conflicts.notes: Real chore-avoidance in a family-event context, distinct setting from home.

conflicts.name: A younger cousin copies everything you do at a gathering
conflicts.notes: Common, relatable sibling/cousin-dynamic irritation.

conflicts.name: Long car/travel ride with nothing to do
conflicts.notes: Real travel-specific patience scenario, distinct from cf_004's generic waiting.

conflicts.name: Forgetting to pack something important for a trip
conflicts.notes: Real travel-preparation responsibility scenario.

conflicts.name: Being scared during a thunderstorm at night
conflicts.notes: Distinct from cf_007 (dark) — storm-specific, tawakkul-compatible.

conflicts.name: A teacher assigns a difficult task and character wants to give up
conflicts.notes: Direct school-context perseverance scenario.

conflicts.name: Two friends both want to lead the same game
conflicts.notes: Real peer-negotiation scenario, distinct from cf_015 (game choice) — here it's about leadership/turns, not game type.

conflicts.name: Being offered something haram-adjacent innocently by a friend (e.g. food with unclear ingredients)
conflicts.notes: Real, age-appropriate values scenario — must not become a food-shaming moment, framed gently as 'checking first.'

conflicts.name: A sibling gets praised for something you also did quietly
conflicts.notes: Real recognition/fairness-adjacent sibling dynamic, distinct from cf_022 (attention on new sibling).

conflicts.name: Wanting to keep playing with new friend's toy a bit too long
conflicts.notes: Borrowed-item boundary scenario, distinct from cf_002/cf_014.

conflicts.name: Wanting to skip prayer to finish watching something
conflicts.notes: Distinct from cf_032 (play) — screen-time specific temptation.

conflicts.name: A grandparent moves slowly and character feels impatient walking with them
conflicts.notes: Real, gentle mercy-toward-elders scenario.

conflicts.name: Parents say no to something reasonable-seeming and character feels it's unfair
conflicts.notes: Distinct from cf_041 — about accepting a decision, not chores.

conflicts.name: Waiting your turn in a long line at the mosque or store
conflicts.notes: Real, distinct public-setting waiting scenario.

conflicts.name: A friend is mean to a smaller or younger child
conflicts.notes: Real bystander-intervention scenario, gentle framing.

conflicts.name: Wanting to donate a favorite (not just spare) toy
conflicts.notes: Distinct from cf_034 — giving something genuinely valued, not surplus.

conflicts.name: Parents ask for help right when character finally has free time
conflicts.notes: Real timing-conflict scenario, distinct from other chore conflicts.

conflicts.name: A charity collection box passes around and character has little to give
conflicts.notes: Real scenario about giving what you can, not comparing amounts.

conflicts.name: Character must be patient through a boring but necessary appointment
conflicts.notes: Distinct setting (doctor/errand) from other waiting conflicts.

conflicts.name: An elderly neighbor needs help carrying groceries
conflicts.notes: Real, concrete mercy-in-action scenario, new setting (neighborhood).

metadata.note: Expanded from 30 to 50 (2026-08-05) — each checked against the existing 30 for setting/situation duplication before adding; new entries specifically fill gaps for concepts that had no story hook (prayer, cleanliness, good_speech, community, courage variants, perseverance, humility). Creative structural data — no web research needed.
